name: GridPatch Electrical Crew Dayside Full Kit
description: The daily rig of a GridPatch Infrastructure electrical maintenance crew member — the people who keep Meridian's power grid from folding under the city's perpetual load. The foundation is a flame-resistant (FR-rated) work shirt in sun-faded mustard yellow, long-sleeve, with pearl-snap closures rather than metal buttons to reduce arc hazard, double chest pockets with snap flaps, and a GridPatch utility patch embroidered on the left chest. The shirt's right cuff has been pre-modified with a velcro breakaway closure, a standard accommodation for workers with chrome forearm augmentation who need to quickly expose hardware. Over this, a lightweight FR-rated vest in charcoal with a mesh back panel for ventilation, four front pockets, and a broad strip of retroreflective tape across the upper back. The vest's rear collar has a reinforced loop for attaching a hardhat retention strap. Trousers are heavy-duty FR canvas in tan, straight-cut with gusseted crotch for full movement, a hammer loop on the left thigh, and multiple cargo pockets sealed with metal-free hook-and-loop closures. Boots are insulated, dielectric-rated (non-conductive) lace-up work boots in brown leather-analog with a composite (non-metal) toe cap. A yellow hard hat with a GridPatch decal rides on the head on-site, clipped to the vest when off. Nitrile-coated work gloves tuck into the vest pocket when not worn.
functionality: full flame-resistant construction, dielectric non-conductive boot, composite non-metal toe cap, breakaway velcro cuff for chrome arm accommodation, metal-free hardware throughout to reduce arc hazard, hardhat retention loop, retroreflective hi-vis strip, ventilated vest back panel, tool loops
what_it_says: Electrical infrastructure work is one of the more respected Circuit trades — technically demanding and genuinely dangerous. This kit marks the wearer as someone with a specialty, not just a body filling a shift. The sun-faded yellow of the shirt says years on the job; the immaculate condition of the dielectric boots says they haven't gotten careless yet.
manufacturer: GridPatch Infrastructure Services (vest, hard hat, gloves — issued) / independent FR workwear suppliers (shirt, trousers, boots — personal purchase, company-spec required)
price_range: Φ250–Φ380 (FR-rated materials carry a premium; boots alone Φ90–Φ130)
story_hooks: A crew member's dielectric boots have been tampered with — the non-conductive sole compromised in a way that looks like wear but isn't, and they're scheduled to work a live substation tomorrow.

The GridPatch vest's pocket contains an inspection report that was never filed — documenting a section of grid infrastructure that is critically degraded and has been signed off as stable by someone up the chain.
The breakaway cuff on the right sleeve keeps triggering at the wrong moment, exposing a chrome forearm that carries illegal modification — military-grade actuators that no Circuit worker should have.
related_entities: Ouroboros Energy Power Distribution Trunk Network

physical_description.visual_profile: High-visibility utility silhouette optimized for industrial electrical work. The wearer appears competent, grounded, and marked by the GLMZ's essential infrastructure class. Sun-faded mustard yellow forms the visual anchor, grounded by tan canvas and charcoal mesh. The retroreflective tape catches light like a safety beacon. This is the uniform of someone who keeps the city's nervous system alive.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, functional, movement-prioritized. The shirt drapes loosely over the chest for air circulation under load. The vest sits unstructured over the shirt. Trousers cut straight and roomy through the leg with a gusseted crotch for crouching and climbing. Boots anchor the frame with solid, non-negotiable stance. Everything sized for layering and rapid augment access.
physical_description.primary_material: FR-rated aramid blend shirt and vest (flame-resistant to 600°F); FR canvas trousers in tan; brown leather-analog work boots with composite toe; nitrile-coated cotton gloves. All materials selected to survive arc flash, thermal stress, and electrical contact without conducting.
physical_description.texture: The shirt has a slight weave texture, softened by repeated washing and sun exposure. The vest mesh is open-weave, airy. Canvas trousers carry a broken-in, slightly stiff hand. Boots are utilitarian matte leather-analog with textured grip soles. Nitrile gloves have a slightly tacky, non-slip grip surface. Retroreflective tape has a subtle prismatic shimmer.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sun-faded mustard yellow (shirt) as primary; charcoal gray (vest) as secondary; tan canvas (trousers); brown leather-analog (boots). Bright yellow hard hat with GridPatch decal. Retroreflective tape in safety white/silver across upper back. No bright accent colors—all choices driven by visibility and thermal safety, not fashion.
physical_description.closures: Pearl-snap closures on shirt (arc-safe). Velcro breakaway on right cuff (augment accommodation). Metal-free hook-and-loop on trouser cargo pockets. Lace-up dielectric boots. Hard hat clips to vest retention loop via metal-free strap.
distinctive_features: GridPatch utility patch embroidered on left chest pocket
Pre-modified right cuff velcro breakaway for chrome augmentation access
Mesh back panel on vest for heat dissipation during summer shifts
Broad retroreflective safety tape across upper back (visibility in grid substations and tunnels)
Reinforced collar loop for hard hat retention strap
Double-pocket design on shirt (practical storage for tools, components, permits)
Gusseted crotch in trousers (designed for climbing and crawling through maintenance shafts)
Composite toe cap on boots (non-conductive, won't spark against metal grates)
Dielectric rating on boots (electrical hazard protection)
All metal hardware replaced with metal-free alternatives
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — working-class functional. This is the uniform of essential infrastructure labor, neither discardable nor compensated at corporate rates. GridPatch-issued vest and hard hat signal employment stability. Personal-purchase components (shirt, trousers, boots) show quality consciousness within budget constraints — the wearer knows their job can kill them.
physical_description.cultural_context: Electrical maintenance crew member for GridPatch Infrastructure Services. Marks the wearer as someone who understands power systems, augmentation compatibility, and industrial safety protocols. A visible grid-keeper in a city dependent on uninterrupted current. The worn appearance and practical modifications signal years of field experience, not green naïveté.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and field-worn. The mustard shirt shows UV fading and minor scuff marks from tool belts and equipment contact. The vest has been patched once or twice on the mesh panel. Trousers bear stains and scuffs that won't come out—grease, concrete dust, trace copper oxides. Boots are scuffed but maintained (work boots are expensive and footwear failures in electrical work are fatal). The hard hat has minor impact marks. Everything is cleanable but shows honest use.

image_prompt: A weathered electrical maintenance worker in full GridPatch dayside kit stands against the interior of a dimly-lit power distribution substation, red warning lights casting amber shadows across sun-faded mustard shirt and charcoal mesh vest. The hard hat with GridPatch decal sits firmly on their head. Retroreflective safety tape glows white where a portable work light catches it. Their boots grip a metal grate floor with confident stance. Industrial cables and transformer equipment loom in soft focus behind. Moody industrial lighting, cool shadows meeting warm work lights. Fine detail on fabric texture—frayed cuff, canvas wear patterns, glove nitrile texture. The wearer appears mid-shift, capable, essential. --ar 2:3 --v 6
